text:
Alex Laferriere has a bigger job in Los Angeles this season. He's playing 19:27 a night, up from 18:19, and he's been on the ice for 69% of the Kings' power-play chances after 30% last season. In his last ten games he's up to 20.5 minutes.

He's using it. His own chances are up to 1.44 expected goals per 60 from 0.96, and the Kings take 56.9% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice, 11 points better than without him. He also has 42 hits.

What's missing is the finish. He has 3 goals on 7.0 expected, shooting 6.8%. He put seven shots on goal twice in his last four games, and the second time, against Pittsburgh on Nov. 7, one went in on the power play. Goals tend to follow chances like these. Fifteen games is a small sample and ice time settles faster than scoring does, but the role is the thing we'd watch, and so far it's sticking.
headline: Laferriere's bigger job is real, the goals are due
